title: lore's graph cache leaves read-only directories that block deleting a worktree
description:
A `lore` run inside a git worktree leaves `.lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations/<hash>` as `dr-xr-xr-x` (read-only). `git worktree remove` then UNREGISTERS the worktree but fails with "Permission denied", leaving the whole checkout on disk with no git state behind it. Observed directly on lore-cli's own review worktrees (-577, -577-r2, -669) and reported for quest-cli's -615 and opum-cli's -392. opum-fleet's OFLE-313 tracks the leftover folders fleet-side.

HELD, no code, do not start. Two things make it worse than a tidiness bug: (a) the failure is SILENT about the leftover — `git worktree list` stops showing it, so the directory looks like clutter rather than a residue of a command that half-succeeded; (b) the DEC-158 ownership guard refuses a session any write inside a worktree path ("may write only inside its declared roots"), so even a session that KNOWS about the leftover cannot chmod or rm it by hand, which is why the standard cleanup recipe in the repository notes does not clear them here.
